 Ct. No. 06
 Sl No. 102
 S.De
 C.R.M. (Db) 2961 of 2024

In Re: - An application for bail under Section 439 of the   Criminal Procedure corresponding to Section 483 of the Bha  Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 in connection with Newtown P  Case No. 200 dated June 28, 2023 under Sections  342/506/376(2)(f)/376(3) of the Indian Penal Code read wit  of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
And  In the matter of: XXXXXX.
 Mr. Navanil De,
 Mr. Srinjan Ghosh, ...for the Petitioner.
 Mr. Bibaswan Bhattacharyya,
 Ms. Debadrita Mondal, ....for the Stat  1.
Petitioner is the step-father of the victim girl.
It is contended due to enmity between her mother and her former husband i.e. the biological father of the child, petitioner has been falsely implicated.
Victim has already been examined.
Possibility of false implication is to be assessed during trial.
2. Under such circumstances we are inclined to grant bail.

3. Accordingly, we direct the petitioner viz. XXXXX shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Judge, Special Court (under POCSO Act), Barasat, 24- Parganas

subject to the condition that the petitioner shall appear before the trial court on each and every date of hearing until further orders and shall not intimidate witnesses and/or tamper with evidence in any manner whatsoever.
4. In the event petitioner fails to appear before the Trial Court without any justifiable cause, the Trial Court shall be at liberty to cancel his bail without any further reference to this Court.

Signed By :
SANDIP DE High Court of Calcutta 18 th of September 2024 01:49:31 PM

(Gaurang Kanth, J.) (Joymalya Bagchi,

In the matter of : Xxxxxx ......Appellant/
 Applicant.

Mr. Deepak Prahladka,
 Ms. Reshmi Khatoon ......for the Appellant/Applicant.

Mr. Jaydeep Biswas,
 Mr. Sachit Talukdar .......for the State.
Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J.
In re : CRAN 2 of 2026 1.
Service Report filed by the State, be kept with the records.
In spite of service, nobody appears for the victim / defacto complainant.
2. The petitioner was convicted under Section 376 (2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for ten years.
He says that he has already served out six years.
He prays for suspension of sentence.
3. The petitioner says that the charge leveled against him is completely false.
The victim girl refused to allow DNA test of the child.
Hence, there is no evidence that the child that the victim girl gave birth to, is the petitioner's child.
The paper book is not ready.
There is no chance of an early hearing of the present appeal.
Hence, his prayer should be allowed.

4. Learned State Counsel says that although the victim girl refused DNA test of the child, she eloquently described the incident whereby the petitioner, being the stepfather of the victim, violated her.
As a result, she got pregnant.
There is sufficient incriminating evidence against the petitioner.
No leniency should be shown to him.
5. Keeping aside the merits of the case for a moment, we find that the petitioner has served out about 60% of the term sentence of ten years.
From a departmental note dated March 11, 2026, we see that although the department has received the Trial Court Records, the paper book is not ready.
Therefore, nobody can say when this appeal of 2024 will be heard.
Several appeals filed much prior in point of time are yet to be heard.

Xxxxxx vs Unknown on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150138848/
1 6.

On the above considerations and keeping in mind the ratio of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kiran Kumar Vs State of MP reported in (2001) 9 SCC 211, we feel impelled to allow this application and suspend the sentence of imprisonment imposed upon the applicant/
appellant.

entities.text: Kiran Kumar Vs State of MP reported in (2001) 9 SCC 211
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Accordingly, we direct that the applicant/appellant, namely XXXX shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-, with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local,
to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, North 24 Parganas at Barasat, and on further conditions that he shall report to the Inspector in charge/Officer in charge of the jurisdictional police station where he shall be presently residing once in a fortnight till disposal of the appeal and shall not leave the geographical limits of North 24 Parganas until further order.
The petitioner shall not enter the jurisdiction of ECO Park Police Station until further orders and he shall inform his current local address to the learned Trial Court.

The applicant shall be personally present or shall be represented by his Counsel during hearing of the appeal and he shall surrender before the Trial Court as and when called for in connection with the present appeal.

8. The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant/appellant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

9. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
10. The application being CRAN 2 of 2026 is accordingly disposed of.
11. All parties shall act in terms of server copy of the order downloaded from the official website of this Court.
(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.) (Arijit Banerjee, J.)
